terms.grammar: imperative of subveniō, with the dative of the one helped; singular subvenī
terms.comment: “Come to the rescue!”: the plainest cry.

terms.gloss: help, good people! (I appeal to your protection)
terms.grammar: accusative, with obsecrō or implōrō understood or expressed; vostram in Plautus
evidence: Plaut. Rud. 615: vostram ego implōrō fidem
terms.comment: With prō, prō fidem! (Plaut. Amph. 376). The gods’ version, prō deum atque hominum fidem!, is mostly an outburst of indignation (see good heavens!).

phrases.latin: quō rapitis mē? quō fertis mē? periī, opsecrō vestram fidem, Epidamniēnsēs, subvenīte, cīvēs.
phrases.english: Where are you dragging me? where are you carrying me? I’m done for! I beg your help, people of Epidamnus: help, citizens!

phrases.latin: Prō Cȳrēnēnsēs populārēs, vostram ego implōrō fidem
phrases.english: O people of Cyrene, I implore your help

sources: Lewis & Short: subvenio · Lewis & Short: fides · Lewis & Short: prō (interj.)
